subject: math
title: Grade 7 Adding and Subtracting Integers
seo_title: Grade 7 Adding and Subtracting Integers Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Operations with integers (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and order of operations)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on adding and subtracting integers for the BC curriculum: integer tiles and zero pairs, number lines, same and different signs, subtracting by adding the opposite, and word problems with temperatures, depths and bank balances. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: To subtract an integer, add its opposite: 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8.
key_sub: Same signs: add and keep the sign, so −7 + (−5) = −12. Different signs: subtract and use the sign of the number farther from 0, so −3 + 5 = 2, not −8.
body_html:
Zero pairs

A yellow tile is +1 and a red tile is −1. One yellow tile and one red tile make a zero pair: 1 + (−1) = 0. You can add or remove zero pairs without changing the value.

Adding on a number line

Start at the first number. Adding a positive number moves right. Adding a negative number moves left.

Rules for adding

SignsWhat to doExample
Same signsAdd the sizes. Keep the sign.−7 + (−5) = −12
Different signsSubtract the sizes. Use the sign of the number farther from 0.−3 + 5 = 2
Example 1

What is 9 + (−14)?

Different signs: 14 − 9 = 5. −14 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative.

Answer: −5

Subtracting: add the opposite

To subtract an integer, add its opposite. Keep the first number, change − to +, and change the sign of the second number.

Example 2

What is −4 − 6?

Add the opposite: −4 + (−6). Same signs: 4 + 6 = 10, keep the negative sign.

Answer: −10

Example 3

At 6 a.m. in Prince George it was −15 °C. At 2 p.m. it was 3 °C. How much did the temperature rise?

Later − earlier: 3 − (−15) = 3 + 15 = 18.

Answer: 18 degrees

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
−3 + 5 = −8Different signs: subtract the sizes. −3 + 5 = 2
5 − (−3) = 2Add the opposite: 5 + 3 = 8
4 + (−9) = 5Use the sign of the number farther from 0: −5
−6 + (−2) = 8Same signs keep the sign: −8
Counting the starting point as a hopCount the jumps, not the dots

faq.q: How do you add and subtract integers in Grade 7?
faq.a: To add, look at the signs: with the same signs, add and keep the sign; with different signs, subtract and use the sign of the number farther from 0. To subtract, add the opposite: 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8.

faq.q: What is a zero pair in math?
faq.a: A zero pair is one positive tile and one negative tile, because +1 + (−1) = 0. Removing zero pairs does not change the value, so −6 + 4 leaves 2 red tiles, which is −2.

faq.q: Why does subtracting a negative number make the answer bigger?
faq.a: Subtracting is the same as adding the opposite, so 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8. On a number line, 5 is 8 steps to the right of −3.

faq.q: Do these integer worksheets help with the Grade 7 FSA?
faq.a: Yes. Integer operations are part of the BC Grade 7 math curriculum, and the Grade 7 FSA includes numeracy. Problems with temperatures, depths and bank balances, like the ones here, are good practice.

items.q: Chloe models −6 + 4 with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 4 zero pairs and remove them. 2 red tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 6 − 4 = 2. −6 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative. −6 + 4 = −2.

items.q: Jasleen models 5 + (−8) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 5 zero pairs and remove them. 3 red tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 8 − 5 = 3. −8 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative. 5 + (−8) = −3.

items.q: Mateo models −3 + (−4) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: All the tiles are red, so there are no zero pairs. Count them: 7 red tiles. −3 + (−4) = −7.

items.q: Ji-woo models 7 + (−2) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 2 zero pairs and remove them. 5 yellow tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 7 − 2 = 5. 7 is farther from 0, so the answer is positive. 7 + (−2) = 5.

items.q: Harjot models −9 + 5 with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 5 zero pairs and remove them. 4 red tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 9 − 5 = 4. −9 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative. −9 + 5 = −4.

items.q: Olivia wants to show −3 with integer tiles. She starts with 5 red tiles. How many yellow tiles does she need?
items.e: The 5 red tiles show −5. Each yellow tile you add makes a zero pair with a red tile. To get to −3, add 2 yellow tiles: −5 + 2 = −3.

items.q: Noah shows an integer with 10 yellow tiles and 4 red tiles. What integer is it?
items.e: 4 zero pairs are worth 0. With 6 more yellow tiles, the value is 6. So Noah uses 4 + 6 = 10 yellow tiles and 4 red tiles: 10 + (−4) = 6.

items.q: Without calculating, what can you say about −47 + 29?
c: It is positive, because 47 + 29 is positive.
It is negative, because both numbers are negative.
It is positive, because 29 is positive.
It is negative, because −47 is farther from 0.
items.e: The signs are different, so the sum takes the sign of the number farther from 0. 47 > 29, so the sum is negative (it is −18).

items.e: The signs are different, so the sum takes the sign of the number farther from 0. 62 > 35, so the sum is positive (it is 27).

items.e: To subtract, add the opposite. The opposite of −3 is 3, so 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3.

sets.title: Word problems: temperature, depth and money

items.q: At 7 a.m. on a January day in Prince George, the temperature was −16 °C. By noon it had risen 9 degrees. What was the temperature at noon?
items.e: Rising means adding: −16 + 9 = −7 °C.

items.q: In Kelowna, it was 3 °C at 6 p.m. The temperature fell 8 degrees by midnight. What was the temperature at midnight?
items.e: Falling means subtracting: 3 − 8 = 3 + (−8) = −5 °C.

items.q: On the same winter morning, it was 6 °C in Vancouver and −14 °C in Prince George. How many degrees warmer was Vancouver?
items.e: Find the difference: 6 − (−14) = 6 + 14 = 20 degrees. On a number line, 6 to 0 is 6 and 0 to −14 is 14: 6 + 14 = 20.

items.q: At Whistler, the temperature in the village is −3 °C. At the top of the mountain it is 9 degrees colder. What is the temperature at the top?
items.e: Colder means subtracting: −3 − 9 = −3 + (−9) = −12 °C.

items.q: In Prince George, the temperature was −11 °C at 7 a.m. and 2 °C at 3 p.m. How many degrees did the temperature rise?
items.e: Rise = later temperature − earlier temperature: 2 − (−11) = 2 + 11 = 13 degrees.

items.q: A freezer is set to −18 °C and a fridge is set to 4 °C. What is the difference between the two temperatures?
items.e: 4 − (−18) = 4 + 18 = 22 degrees. Subtracting a negative means adding its opposite.

items.q: Owen is scuba diving in Howe Sound at −12 m. He swims up 5 m. What is his new position?
items.e: Up means adding: −12 + 5 = −7 m. He is still below sea level.

items.q: Wei is diving at −8 m off Vancouver Island. He goes down another 9 m to look at a rockfish. What is his new position?
items.e: Down means subtracting: −8 − 9 = −8 + (−9) = −17 m.

items.q: Ryan is diving at −6 m and Hana is diving at −14 m. How far apart are they?
items.e: Subtract the positions: −6 − (−14) = −6 + 14 = 8 m. Both are below sea level, so the distance is 14 − 6.

items.q: Mount Robson, the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies, is 3954 m above sea level. A diver is at −20 m. How much higher is the top of Mount Robson than the diver?
items.e: 3954 − (−20) = 3954 + 20 = 3974 m. Count 20 m up to sea level, then 3954 m more.

items.q: A robot submarine is exploring the ocean off Haida Gwaii at −85 m. It rises 35 m. What is its new position?
items.e: Rising means adding: −85 + 35 = −50 m.

items.q: Sofia has $25 in her bank account. She buys a $40 hockey stick with her debit card, and the account goes below zero. What is the balance now?
items.e: Spending means subtracting: 25 − 40 = 25 + (−40) = −$15. She owes the bank $15.

items.q: Ava’s bank balance is −$30. She deposits $50 of birthday money. What is the balance now?
items.e: A deposit means adding: −30 + 50 = $20.

items.q: Lucas’s balance is −$12. He deposits $20, then spends $15 at a Kamloops sports store. What is the balance now?
In a Burnaby parkade, the ground floor is level 0 and the levels below it are −1, −2, and so on. Zara parks on level −3 and takes the elevator up to level 4. How many levels does she go up?
items.e: 4 − (−3) = 4 + 3 = 7 levels. Count 3 levels up to 0, then 4 more.

items.q: Arjun gets on the elevator in a Surrey building on level 5. He goes down 7 levels to the parkade. Which level is he on now?
items.e: Down means subtracting: 5 − 7 = 5 + (−7) = −2.

items.q: In a class trivia game, a right answer is +10 points and a wrong answer is −15 points. A team has −20 points and then gets one wrong answer. What is the team’s score now?
items.e: A wrong answer adds −15: −20 + (−15) = −35.

items.q: In hockey, a player’s plus-minus goes up 1 when the player’s team scores while the player is on the ice and down 1 when the other team scores. Ethan’s plus-minus is −1. In the next game, his team scores 2 goals and the other team scores 5 while he is on the ice. What is his plus-minus now?
In Prince George, the temperature dropped 12 degrees overnight. In the morning it was −20 °C. What was the temperature the evening before?
items.e: Work backwards: the evening temperature was 12 degrees warmer. −20 + 12 = −8 °C.

items.q: In one week in Prince George, the highest temperature was 5 °C and the lowest was −23 °C. What is the difference between the highest and lowest temperatures?
items.e: 5 − (−23) = 5 + 23 = 28 degrees. From −23 up to 0 is 23 degrees, and 0 up to 5 is 5 more.
